reading_notes: This is an English letter opening, addressed “Dear Kostant,” and dated 22 October 1969. The handwritten place remains uncertain as Massy. There is no author page number or total page count; 21 is the archive foliation.

The writer says that Brieskorn’s work on Klein singularities prompted rereading two papers of Kostant, requests later reprints, and proposes reconsidering the work within algebraic geometry. The two paper names are references quoted within the letter, not a title supplied for the sheet.

L09–L17 propose classifying quadruples (T,B,T′,B′) in a complex simple adjoint Lie group, with the tori in apposition and the Borel subgroups containing them. The source writes the counts as card(W)^2/hzφ(h) and, after adding a generating element of T∩N(T′), card(W)^2/hz. These assertions are transcribed without checking them or silently changing denominator scope.
L18–L19 assert T∩T′=e and describe the resulting structure as rigid up to exterior automorphisms. The text uses the misspelling stablity; it is retained.

L20–L26 ask whether some or all such quadruples have opposite Borel subgroups, whether a distinguished conjugacy class exists that is invariant under exterior automorphisms, and what their automorphism groups are. The last question continues beyond this sheet; it is not completed here.

The bottom note asserts an extension description for N(T)∩N(T′), involving (Z/hZ)^* and Z/hZ times the central factor, and gives order hzφ(h). The separate annotation “center of G with tilde” is linked to the final Z. The heavily canceled suffix after Z remains uncertain.

Source corrections and slips remain visible: doubtful Maer./Amer.; original polynomail plus its transposition mark; suggests number without an added article; extra canceled letters in both quadruples occurrences; an with deleted n; and the corrected title initial. No external bibliography, place information or mathematical proof was used to regularize them.
